svg.title: Shoga-Speaks: Claude Code, explained for you
svg.desc: A before and after in a Claude Code terminal. Four people ask about the same payment bug, each in their own language and role. Without Shoga-Speaks the reply is a wall of jargon. Shoga the parakeet flies over from the logo and pecks the Shoga-Speaks switch on: the wall folds into a short answer in their language, with the technical detail tucked under Technical and a hard word explained on click.

g.text: Great question! This is a classic non-deterministic, timing-dependent concurrency
defect (a race condition). Below is a complete root-cause analysis with traces.
## 1. What is happening
A race condition: two concurrent POST /payments/charge requests for the same order both
read status='pending' before either commits, so both proceed to capture the payment.
## 2. Reconstructed trace (failing run #4471)
T+0.000ms req#A BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED idempotency_key=NULL
T+0.412ms req#B BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED idempotency_key=NULL
T+1.207ms req#A SELECT status FROM orders WHERE id=$1 -> 'pending'
T+1.344ms req#B SELECT status FROM orders WHERE id=$1 -> 'pending' !! stale read
T+9.880ms req#A gateway.capture({amount: 4999, currency}) -> cap_81f2 OK
T+10.02ms req#B gateway.capture({amount: 4999, currency}) -> cap_81f9 OK !! duplicate
T+11.73ms req#A UPDATE orders SET status='paid' -> 1 row COMMIT
T+11.90ms req#B UPDATE orders SET status='paid' -> 1 row COMMIT (lost update)
## 3. Why the test is flaky, not always red
- jest runs suites in parallel workers (--maxWorkers=50%); scheduling order varies per run
- the mocked gateway resolves in 3-14 ms, so the race window opens in ~31% of runs
- retry middleware: 3 attempts, exponential backoff 200/400/800 ms, re-enters charge()
- the webhook 'payment.captured' may arrive before COMMIT; at-least-once delivery
## 4. Isolation levels (PostgreSQL semantics)
READ COMMITTED dirty read: no non-repeatable: yes phantom: yes lost update: yes
REPEATABLE READ dirty read: no non-repeatable: no phantom: no serialization error
SERIALIZABLE SSI predicate locks; expect 40001 retries under contention
## 5. Remediation options
a) pessimistic lock SELECT ... FROM orders WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE
b) optimistic lock UPDATE orders SET version = version + 1 WHERE id = $1 AND version = $2
c) advisory lock SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1::text))
d) distributed mutex SET lock:order:{id} <uuid> NX PX 30000 (fencing token caveats)
e) idempotency key UNIQUE (merchant_id, idempotency_key) + 24h response replay cache
f) webhook dedupe processed_events(event_id PK) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
## 6. Stack trace
at chargeCustomer (src/payments/charge.ts:88:17)
at async Promise.all (index 1)
at async submitCheckout (src/checkout/submit.ts:142:5)
at async Object.<anonymous> (test/payments.spec.ts:57:3)
x charges once per order (31 ms) Expected: 1 Received: 2
## 7. Trade-off matrix
option latency throughput complexity multi-region blast radius recommended
a) +2 ms -4% low no row partial
b) +0 ms -0% medium yes row partial
e)+f) +1 ms -1% medium yes request yes
Before choosing, consider CAP implications, clock skew, and the exactly-once fallacy...
... +287 lines (ctrl+r to expand)
